question: The popular folk art of Phad painting is traditionally associated with which of the following Indian states?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Phad paintings** are large scroll paintings, typically depicting **heroic deeds** and **mythological stories** of local deities such as **Pabuji** and **Devnarayan**.
 
• **Phad artists** use natural colors extracted from vegetables, flowers, and minerals to create vibrant and long-lasting artwork, showcasing their skill and craftsmanship.
 
• The art form has been preserved and passed down through generations by traditional artist communities, known as **Joshi families**, who are experts in Phad painting.
 
• **Phad paintings** are created using **natural dyes**, giving them a distinct and earthy look. These dyes are made from organic materials such as **vegetables, flowers, and minerals**.
 
• Phad paintings are traditionally used as **storytelling tools** by itinerant priests and performers, known as **Bhopa** and **Bhopi**.
 
• **Example**: Stories of **Pabuji**, a local folk hero worshipped as a deity, are commonly depicted in Phad paintings. These stories are narrated in villages during religious and cultural gatherings.

 
• **Preservation of Art:**

 
 
• Renowned artists like **Shree Lal Joshi**, a Padma Shri awardee, have contributed significantly to revitalizing Phad painting and spreading its popularity worldwide.
 
• Phad paintings are traditionally made on **hand-woven cloth**, using **vegetable dyes**. The process can take several weeks to complete.
 
• **Madhya Pradesh:** Known for **Gond paintings**, depicting nature and tribal stories.
 
• **Gujarat:** Renowned for **Pithora paintings**, a tribal art form symbolizing prosperity.
